burials.name: Township and village clerks / sextons
burials.what: Most Cass County cemeteries are owned by the townships (or the village/city); burial and lot records sit with the township clerk or sexton. The Cass County MIGenWeb page notes that township officials, not volunteers, handle lots. Reach a township through its own office (township halls are listed on the county website). Example: Prospect Hill Cemetery in Cassopolis is owned and operated by the Village of Cassopolis, (269) 445-8648, manager@cassopolis-mi.us.

burials.name: Cass District Library, Local History Branch - cemetery indexes
burials.what: Holds the DAR (Capt. Samuel Felt Chapter) index of Cass County cemeteries made in the late 1930s-early 1940s, plus published township/cemetery indexes (e.g., Silver Creek Twp. 1994, Wayne Twp. 1994, Jefferson Twp. 1996, Young's Prairie 1996 with burial permits and sexton records). Printed, viewed at the branch (145 N. Broadway, Cassopolis; Mon-Thu 9-4; (269) 357-7823). Research guide PDF online; a second PDF lists additional indexes.

burials.name: Cass District Library - additional cemetery indexes list
burials.what: PDF list of further Cass County cemetery indexes in the Local History Branch (seen in search results; title only verified).

burials.name: DAR 'Cass County, Michigan cemetery records' (Capt. Samuel Felt Chapter)
burials.what: Compiled DAR cemetery readings; on microfilm at the Library of Michigan, Lansing (call no. F574.O847 C4 1980a), per the Library of Michigan Cass County guide.

burials.name: Cass County MIGenWeb - Cemeteries
burials.what: Volunteer index of about 71 cemeteries across 15 townships, marked active/retired/abandoned; most link to burial listings drawn from 1940s DAR readings and later volunteer readings; also sells transcribed cemetery books. Site warns listings may be incomplete.

burials.name: MIGenWeb Tombstone Photo Project - Cass County
burials.what: Volunteer headstone photographs by cemetery (e.g., Prospect Hill, Cassopolis).

burials.name: Library of Michigan - cemetery transcripts
burials.what: The state library in Lansing holds cemetery transcripts for Michigan counties among its family-history collections.

burials.name: Find a Grave / BillionGraves
burials.what: Both volunteer memorial/headstone databases cover Cass County cemeteries (not read here; Find a Grave sits behind a bot check).

burials.what: Free index of cemetery transcriptions by Michigan county; check for Cass County entries.

burials.name: VA Nationwide Gravesite Locator
burials.what: U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs search for burial places of veterans and family members in national, state veterans' and some other cemeteries; last name required.

obituaries.name: Cass District Library - Local Newspaper Obituary Indexes
obituaries.what: PDF name indexes to obituaries in local papers (file names cite the Cassopolis Vigilant, Edwardsburg Argus and Marcellus News).
obituaries.years: 1998-2012 (one combined file; its filename says 2008-2012) then one PDF per year 2013-2025
obituaries.how: Indexes are free online; the papers themselves are on microfilm at the Local History Branch, 145 N. Broadway, Cassopolis. No copy-request form or fee is posted - call (269) 357-7823 or (866) 808-7323, or email the branch through the address on its page.

obituaries.name: Southwest Michigan Obituary Index (Van Buren Regional Genealogical Society)
obituaries.what: Name index of over 89,000 obituaries for Allegan, Berrien, Cass, Kalamazoo and Van Buren counties, citing the Herald-Palladium, Kalamazoo Gazette, South Bend Tribune, Niles Daily Star, funeral records and other sources; each entry gives date, source code and page.
obituaries.how: By mail: $3.00 per item (check, cash or money order) with a self-addressed stamped envelope and the full index entry, to VBRGS, P.O. Box 143, Decatur, MI 49045 (terms as posted on the index page; confirm before sending).

obituaries.name: Cass District Library - Connelly Funeral Home records

obituaries.how: Free PDFs online; originals at the Local History Branch.

obituaries.name: Cassopolis Vigilant microfilm guide

obituaries.how: Use at the Local History Branch.

obituaries.how: Visit in Lansing or ask via Librarian@Michigan.gov / 517-335-1477.

walk.name: Prospect Hill Cemetery
walk.why: The county seat's cemetery; first recorded burial 7 August 1832, incorporated 1879; maps are posted by the village, and volunteers flag veterans' graves for Memorial Day.

notes: No active county-wide genealogical society with cemetery publications could be confirmed; the Cass District Library Local History Branch is the county's main repository. Dowagiac's Riverside Cemetery would be a natural second walk, but its address and history were not verified, so it is left out. FamilySearch catalogs 'Riverside Cemetery records, 1866-1984' (https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/47346 - seen only in a search result). digmichnews.cmich.edu refused automated reading.

walk.name: Silverbrook Cemetery
walk.address: 1400 E. Main St., Niles, MI 49120 (gates at Cherry and Main)
walk.why: Niles's public cemetery since 1836 (George Bond's six acres, lots sold from 1838), now over 60 acres; 1926 gates, abbey and chime tower; burials include Calvin F. Wilson, a charter member of Michigan's first Black Masonic lodge, and the Plym family of Kawneer. Friends of Silverbrook and the Niles History Center run an annual tour (4 Oct 2026) and a virtual tour.

walk.name: Crystal Springs Cemetery
walk.address: Napier Avenue (between Pipestone Rd. and Crystal Ave.), Benton Township, near Benton Harbor
walk.why: Founded in 1893 by the City of Benton Harbor; grew from 30 to over 110 acres, landscaped under superintendent Herman Vogt (1921-53), with the Tower of Remembrance bell tower; Calvary (Catholic) and a Jewish cemetery adjoin it.

notes: Niles District Library's archive page (nileslibrary.com/archives) did not load, so the early Niles papers are listed from the Clarke portal only. The SW Michigan Obituary Index ordering terms come from the index page; the society should be asked whether mail orders are still taken. No public obituary index at the St. Joseph (Maud Preston Palenske) or Benton Harbor libraries could be confirmed.

walk.name: Lake View Cemetery
walk.address: South Haven, MI (city-owned; Section 2 per MIGenWeb - street address not verified)
walk.why: South Haven's pioneer cemetery: lighthouse keeper James Donahue, early woman physician Marion Low, lumberman John Mackey, photographer Nanna Brown, Medal of Honor recipient William H. obituaries.how: View full records at Local & Family History Services, Main Library 3rd floor, 304 S. Main St., South Bend. Remote/homebound: online Research Request form or printable PDF (linked from sjcpl.org/lfh); 'there may be a charge' - no fee posted. local.history@sjcpl.org, 574-282-4621.

obituaries.name: SJCPL Local & Family History - newspaper clipping files and databases
obituaries.what: Print clipping files (1920s-1960s full, 1970s-2000s partial), newspaper collection index, microfilm, newspaper databases, and the Michiana Memory digital collection.
obituaries.how: In person or by research request.

obituaries.name: St. Joseph County INGenWeb - obituary index
obituaries.what: Volunteer index of over 15,000 obituaries.
obituaries.how: Free online.

obituaries.name: SBAGS newspaper indexes
obituaries.what: Genealogical Index to Victorian-era St. Joseph County newspapers (1875-1913), Mishawaka Enterprise index and vital statistics index (1982-2003), Coroner's Records Index (1879-1960).
obituaries.how: Online (some SBAGS content is members-only); contact via sbags.org/contact-us.

obituaries.name: Michiana Genealogical Index (SBAGS)
obituaries.what: Free surname index (Norbert Cramer) of births, deaths, marriages and cemetery sources drawn mainly from area newspapers.
obituaries.how: Free online search.

obituaries.name: Hoosier State Chronicles (Indiana State Library)
obituaries.what: Free digitized Indiana newspapers, over a million pages 1804-2018. The site refused automated reading (robots), so county titles were not checked.
obituaries.how: Free online.

deaths.name: Indiana death certificates 1899-2011 (Ancestry)
deaths.what: Statewide death certificates with images and index, filed 1899-2011, from Indiana State Board of Health records on microfilm at the Indiana Archives and Records Administration. The Indiana State Archives says unofficial copies 'may be obtained on Ancestry.com'; the Indiana State Library lists it as available free in the library and statewide via Ancestry Library Edition. A free FamilySearch copy of the certificates was NOT confirmed.

deaths.name: Indiana State Archives (IARA) - vital records guidance
deaths.what: For 1882-1906 deaths, contact the county health office where the death occurred; 1907 and later from the Indiana Department of Health (orderable online). The Indiana State Library Genealogy Division holds WPA death indexes for about half the counties.

deaths.name: Indiana Death Index 1882-1920 (FamilySearch)
deaths.what: Free index covering 67 of 92 counties, per the Indiana State Library.

deaths.name: SBAGS Coroner's Records Index 1879-1960
deaths.what: Index to St. Joseph County coroner's records.

walk.name: South Bend City Cemetery
walk.address: 214 Elm Street (at Colfax), South Bend, IN 46616
walk.why: South Bend's oldest cemetery (land given by Lathrop Taylor and Alexis Coquillard; first burial 1831), 21 acres, about 14,800 burials, listed on the National Register in 2018. Graves include Vice President Schuyler Colfax, the Studebaker brothers (Clement, John, Peter), President McKinley's paternal grandparents, and Medal of Honor recipient Enoch R. Weiss.

notes: Founding date given as 1832 by Venues Parks & Arts, with the first burial in 1831 per Wikipedia. SJCPL copy fees not posted. Hoosier State Chronicles refused automated reading. The brief's 'Indiana death certificates on FamilySearch' could not be confirmed - only the 1882-1920 index is on FamilySearch per the Indiana State Library.

burials.name: City of Elkhart Cemetery Department
burials.what: Runs Rice (400 James St.), Grace Lawn and Prairie Street cemeteries; helps locate hard-to-find burials and handles genealogy requests; holds the list of people moved from the old Middlebury Street cemetery. Contacts: charles.choate@coei.org, hannah.colbourn@coei.org.

burials.name: City of Goshen Department of Cemeteries - Goshen Cemetery Explorer
burials.what: Oakridge, West Goshen, Violett and Dierdorff cemeteries; the online Cemetery Explorer map locates burials (Violett reviewed; Oakridge and West Goshen still in quality control). Office Mon-Fri 7-3, 574-534-5306; 202 S. 5th St., Goshen.

burials.name: Elkhart County Genealogical Society (ECGS)
burials.what: Compiled 'Cemeteries of Elkhart County, Indiana' (vols. I-III, 1991; an older guide says four volumes), with a free online name index on the INGenWeb site; sells by mail funeral-home indexes and Burial Transit Permits for Elkhart City 1950-1984 and County 1950-1982 (prices on its page, last updated c. 2013 - confirm). P.O. Box 1031, Elkhart, IN 46515-1031. Its library (Sailor Memorial Library) is listed at the Rush Memorial Center, 304 W. Vistula St., Bristol, Tue-Fri 10-2.

burials.name: Online Index of Cemeteries of Elkhart County, Vols. I-III
burials.what: Name index to the ECGS cemetery books, on Elkhart County INGenWeb (page not opened; listed on the INGenWeb home page). INGenWeb also links Patricia Johnson's county cemetery list and the Indiana Pioneer Cemeteries Restoration Project page for Elkhart County.

burials.name: Library cemetery indexes
burials.what: Elkhart Public Library and Goshen Public Library both hold Cemeteries of Elkhart County plus indexes to Grace Lawn, Rice, Prairie Street, Oakridge, Violett and West Goshen cemeteries and 'Tombstone Records of Elkhart County'.

burials.name: Interment.net - Clinton Union Cemetery, Goshen
burials.what: Transcription linked from INGenWeb; Interment.net's Indiana index may have more county sets.

burials.name: Indiana DNR Cemetery & Burial Ground Registry (CBGR)
burials.what: State registry of all Indiana cemeteries and burial grounds kept by the Division of Historic Preservation & Archaeology: location, marker count, condition, affiliations, veterans, features (not a list of names). Searchable inside SHAARD and shown on the IHBBC map.

burials.name: Indiana State Library - Cemetery Locator Index
burials.what: Statewide catalog of Indiana cemeteries by county and township with legal location and the State Library call numbers of books that list each one.

burials.name: Find a Grave / BillionGraves
burials.what: Both volunteer memorial/headstone databases cover the county's cemeteries (not read here; Find a Grave sits behind a bot check).

burials.name: VA Nationwide Gravesite Locator
burials.what: U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs search for burial places of veterans and family members in national, state veterans' and some other cemeteries; last name required.

obituaries.name: Elkhart Public Library - Elkhart Truth obituary index
obituaries.what: Searchable citation index to Elkhart Truth obituaries (by date range, last, first and maiden name).
obituaries.years: not stated on the page (a 1998-era guide described the file as 1980s-1990s)
obituaries.how: Read the papers at the downtown library, 300 S. Second St. Remote requests via the research form: $5 per 30 minutes (covers 1-3 obituary requests), paid in advance, charged whether or not found, one request per person per month, SASE for mail (https://www.myepl.org/assistance/). reference@myepl.org, 574-522-5669.

obituaries.name: Goshen Public Library - obituary indexes
obituaries.what: Card file 1970-1994 (obituaries and anniversaries); index 1994-2007 at the reference desk; Goshen News index 2007-present. Goshen newspapers 1837-2022 in the Indiana Room on microfilm; NewspaperARCHIVE access.
obituaries.how: The Reference Department will send a local obituary by mail or email; no fee or form is posted - contact the reference desk.

obituaries.name: Funeral home indexes (Goshen Public Library / ECGS)
obituaries.what: Dale White (Elkhart) 1929-1993; Walley-Mills-Zimmerman 1912-1988 and 1999-2005; Waterman-Westbrook-Clouse 1940-2005; Stemm-Lawson-Peterson (Elkhart 1954-2002, Bristol 1978-2002); Carlyse Wagner (Bristol) 1944-1960.
obituaries.how: Use at the library, or buy ECGS indexes by mail.

obituaries.name: Elkhart County INGenWeb - submitted obituaries
obituaries.what: Volunteer-submitted obituaries.
obituaries.how: Free online.

obituaries.what: Obituary index to the Herald of Truth (1864-1908) and Gospel Herald, per a dated (1998/2016) INGenWeb guide.
obituaries.how: Contact the library at Goshen College.

walk.name: Grace Lawn Cemetery
walk.address: Elkhart, IN (city-owned; street address not on the city page)
walk.why: Dedicated in 1864 and named for Grace Clark, foster daughter of town founder-surveyor Charles Beardsley; early Elkhart families, over 100 Civil War soldiers, burials moved from the old Middlebury Street cemetery, a 1918 gateway and the Baldwin-Beardsley mausoleum.

walk.name: Oakridge Cemetery
walk.why: Burials from 1832, city-owned since 1859, over 40 acres; mayors, Goshen's first postmaster, veterans of every major American war, and GAR, Odd Fellows and Jewish (Sharis Israel) sections.

notes: ECGS's RootsWeb page dates from about 2008-2013; its prices, library location and hours should be confirmed before publishing. Grace Lawn's street address was not on the city page. Elkhart Truth index years not stated by the library.

burials.name: Michigan City Cemetery Department
burials.what: Runs Greenwood (with Sinai, Calvary and Islamic sections), Calvary and Swan Lake Memorial Gardens; official burial records searchable online at swanlake.cemsites.com (gravesite search, maps). Office 5700 E. US Hwy 20, Michigan City; (219) 873-1522; Mon-Fri 7-3:30.

walk.name: Greenwood Cemetery
walk.why: Michigan City's city cemetery, established 1863 and dedicated 1864 by Mayor H. H. Roberts; holds Sinai (Jewish), Calvary (Catholic) and Islamic sections; burials moved from the old city burial ground; the county historical museum has led tours ('History and Mystery at Greenwood', Oct. 2025).

notes: The La Porte County Genealogical Society's RootsWeb page gives no current meeting place or contact beyond Facebook. The Cemetery & Research Association of LaPorte County's website URL was not found (named only on the Michigan City library guide). Pine Lake Cemetery (La Porte, Center Twp., Sec. 22) is in the State Library locator, but no verified address or history was found, so it is not offered as a walk. lcplin.org is the Lake County (not LaPorte) library.
